bibl.title: Neural underpinnings of the evidence accumulator

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: Which brain regions actually compute the gradual accumulation of evidence, as opposed to merely representing its value.
span.quote: To study the macro- and micro-circuitry causally responsible for gradual accumulation, we must first know which brain regions are part of that circuitry.

span.label: critique
span.quote: Consequently, we consider the PPC to have the lowest likelihood of being an important center of the causally relevant circuit for gradual evidence accumulation.

span.label: gradual accumulation of evidence in perceptual decision-making
span.quote: Gradual accumulation of evidence favoring one or another choice is considered a core component of many different types of decisions, and has been the subject of many neurophysiological studies in non-human primates.

span.label: review
span.quote: Here we will first briefly describe studies with non-human primates into the neural basis of the evidence accumulator.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: In this model, when the evidence is strong, the accumulator’s value quickly diverges away from the decision boundary, and it rapidly become easy to say on which side of the decision boundary it is.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: the FOF’s main role in the task lies in categorizing the value of the accumulator, an operation that occurs after the graded evidence accumulation itself

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: the observed effects from inactivations targeting rodent PPC could perhaps be due to inactivation spillover into one of the many small V2 areas

span.label: Encoding was inferred from ramping firing rates that rise faster on easy trials than hard ones, exactly as the accumulator model predicts
span.quote: Critically, when averaged across easy trials, firing rates ramped slowly; but when averaged across difficult trials, firing rates ramped much more sharply--precisely as expected of the evidence accumulator ([ 25 – 27 ]; Fig. 1b ).

span.label: Tuning curves separate two regions that look alike in averages: one reads out the graded value, the other a categorical side of the boundary
span.quote: Thus what is best read out from FOF firing is not the graded value of the accumulator, but rather which categorical decision report the subject should make if the trial ended at that point in time.

span.label: A region can be required at a specific moment rather than throughout, which optogenetic timing can test and lesions cannot
span.quote: The tens of milliseconds time resolution afforded by optogenetic inactivation, in this case using the virally-delivered, light-activated chloride pump eNpHR3.0 [ 52 ] injected unilaterally into the FOF, allowed probing and confirming the hypothesis about the specific times when activity in the FOF would be required (see Fig 2f ; [ 45 ]).

span.label: Microstimulation cannot localise its own effect, because it acts largely on axons passing through rather than on the cells at the site
span.quote: This concern applies to all microstimulation studies, and is consistent with the later claim that microstimulation acts mainly through activation of axons [ 40 ] (but see [ 41 ]).

span.label: The proposed test for circuit membership is three conditions at once - inactivation matters, it matters during the accumulation window specifically, and the graded value is encoded there
span.quote: A region that is part of the relevant causal circuit would be expected to simultaneously satisfy three initial criteria: (1) inactivation of the region should have an effect on task performance.

span.label: Where a label's boundaries are uncertain, an inactivation aimed at one region may be silencing its neighbour, which would reconcile the conflicting results across species
span.quote: With the precise definition of rodent PPC and the location of its border with these V2 areas still highly uncertain and a matter of active research [ 68 – 70 ], the observed effects from inactivations targeting rodent PPC could perhaps be due to inactivation spillover into one of the many small V2 areas.

span.label: The review restricts itself to two-alternative decisions and excludes human work.
span.quote: We limit ourselves to two-alternative decisions (for multi-alternative decisions, see [ 20 ]), and will not address work in humans (see [ 21 ]).

span.label: Whether rats and primates in fact use the same circuits and algorithms for accumulation is inferred from similar ramping responses and is not established.
span.quote: Whether this is indeed the case remains an open question, of course.

span.label: Because the anatomical border of rodent PPC with adjacent small V2 areas is still uncertain, inactivation effects attributed to PPC may reflect spillover into V2.
span.quote: With the precise definition of rodent PPC and the location of its border with these V2 areas still highly uncertain and a matter of active research [ 68 – 70 ], the observed effects from inactivations targeting rodent PPC could perhaps be due to inactivation spillover into one of the many small V2 areas.

span.label: The authors report that their own earlier serial model of the two regions was wrong
span.quote: As we describe below, this serial model turned out to be wrong.

span.label: Neither of the two candidate regions satisfies the criteria the authors themselves propose
span.quote: As described above, neither the FOF nor the PPC satisfy all three criteria.

span.label: A negative inactivation result cannot rule out a redundant circuit in which no single region is required
span.quote: While the PPC could, perhaps, play a role in gradual accumulation as part of a much larger redundant circuit in the Poisson Clicks task, it is notable that out of 6 different rat regions probed so far (medial prefrontal cortex and superior colliculus, (Hanks, Yartsev, et al. unpublished data); anterior dorsal striatum and auditory striatum (Yartsev, Hanks, et al., unpublished data); and FOF and PPC), the only region for which silencing has no impact on task behavior is the PPC.

span.label: The region name itself is unsettled, so results labelled PPC may not concern the same tissue across studies
span.quote: Further clarity on the role of the PPC will greatly benefit from better definitions and knowledge about the topography of brain regions near the location currently referred to as “rodent PPC.”

span.label: Several of the supporting results are unpublished data from the authors' own laboratory
span.quote: Current unpublished data (Yartsev, Hanks, et al.) suggests that while some subcortical regions may be like the FOF in playing an important role in the task, but not in gradual accumulation per se, at least one other subcortical region appears to satisfy all three criteria, and may thus become the first identified node in the causal circuit for evidence accumulation.

span.label: The causal evidence in primates rests on three microstimulation studies, all with the confound the authors name
span.quote: To date, causal perturbation studies of these areas with the primate RDM task have been limited, with only three existing published studies, all using only unilateral electrical microstimulation.

span.label: a region's involvement - ENCODING: the accumulator's graded value can be read out of its firing, which PPC satisfies
span.quote: But while tuning curves in PPC were found to be smooth functions of the value of the accumulator --indicating that the graded value of the accumulator could be read out from PPC firing, as also found in the primate PPC [ 51 ]-- the tuning curves in the FOF were much more step-like, with one cluster of firing rates for accumulator values to one side of the decision boundary, and a different cluster of firing rates for values on the other side of the decision boundary (see Fig. 2e ).

span.label: a region's involvement - CAUSAL: silencing it changes behaviour, which PPC does not satisfy despite encoding the value
span.quote: In contrast to expectations, however, inactivation of the PPC produced entirely negligible effects on performance of the Poisson Clicks task [ 53 ].

span.label: necessity - AT ALL: silencing the region changes performance, criterion one
span.quote: A region that is part of the relevant causal circuit would be expected to simultaneously satisfy three initial criteria: (1) inactivation of the region should have an effect on task performance.

span.label: necessity - AT THE RIGHT TIME: silencing during the accumulation window specifically changes performance, criterion two, which separates accumulating from reading out
span.quote: More specifically, because there are different sequential steps involved in the decision formation and gradual accumulation is only one of them, (2) perturbation during temporally-specific periods that coincide with the evidence accumulation period should impact performance.

span.label: PPC - as a name for tissue defined by location, which differs across labs and species
span.quote: Further clarity on the role of the PPC will greatly benefit from better definitions and knowledge about the topography of brain regions near the location currently referred to as “rodent PPC.”

span.label: PPC - as a name the authors propose reserving for tissue defined by function and connectivity, including the very null result at issue
span.quote: We advocate reserving the name “posterior parietal cortex (PPC)” in rodents to regions displaying physiological and connectivity profiles similar to those of the primate PPC, for example, no impact from inactivation on visual accumulation of evidence tasks [ 55 ], little anatomical input from primary visual cortex [ 71 , 72 ], and strong connectivity with frontal regions, as is the case with the anterior, as opposed to the posterior, zones currently referred to as “rat PPC” [ 70 ].

span.label: builds-on → Brunton et al. (Poisson clicks rat task)
span.quote: To assist in addressing these questions, Brunton et al. developed a rat model of a perceptual decision task dependent on gradual accumulation of evidence (“Poisson clicks” task, [ 42 ]; see also [ 43 , 44 ]).

span.label: critiques → the proposal of a one-to-one relationship between parietal firing rates and the accumulator value
span.quote: Their seminal finding led to the proposal that there may be a 1-to-1 relationship between PPC firing rates and the value of the evidence accumulator.

span.label: critiques → microstimulation as a means of localising causal contributions
span.quote: This concern applies to all microstimulation studies, and is consistent with the later claim that microstimulation acts mainly through activation of axons [ 40 ] (but see [ 41 ]).

span.label: critiques → the authors' own earlier serial model in which PPC computes the accumulator and FOF reads it out
span.quote: More specifically, the analysis suggested a simple serial organization in our fully trained rats, in which the graded value of the accumulator is computed in the PPC, and then read out from there to be turned into a more categorical representation in the FOF; which in turn eventually drives the categorical motor acts with which the animal reports its decision.

span.label: extends → Brunton et al.'s rat Poisson clicks model of accumulation
span.quote: To assist in addressing these questions, Brunton et al. developed a rat model of a perceptual decision task dependent on gradual accumulation of evidence (“Poisson clicks” task, [ 42 ]; see also [ 43 , 44 ]).

span.label: posterior parietal cortex —distinct-from→ evidence accumulation
span.quote: These data suggest that despite its encoding of the graded value of the accumulator, the PPC may play little to no role in decisions driven by accumulation of evidence.

span.label: ramping —operationalised-as→ evidence accumulation
span.quote: Their seminal finding led to the proposal that there may be a 1-to-1 relationship between PPC firing rates and the value of the evidence accumulator.

span.label: frontal orienting fields —causes→ decision boundary
span.quote: This suggests that the FOF may be more strongly involved in categorizing the value of the accumulator to drive the final choice than in computing the graded accumulation itself.

span.label: tuning curves —operationalised-as→ posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: Collating these paired measures across trials allowed building “tuning curves,” plots of average firing rates as a function of the variable of interest, which in this case is the value of the accumulator.

span.label: optogenetic inactivation —contrasted-with→ microstimulation
span.quote: The antidromic activation issue is not a concern with more recent inactivation studies to be described below.

span.label: eNpHR3.0 —operationalised-as→ optogenetic inactivation
span.quote: The tens of milliseconds time resolution afforded by optogenetic inactivation, in this case using the virally-delivered, light-activated chloride pump eNpHR3.0 [ 52 ] injected unilaterally into the FOF, allowed probing and confirming the hypothesis about the specific times when activity in the FOF would be required (see Fig 2f ; [ 45 ]).

span.label: Poisson clicks —contrasted-with→ random dot motion
span.quote: As with the primate RDM task, trial difficulty could be titrated by the experimenters, in this case by controlling the left : right ratio of the Poisson rates that generated the random pulses.

span.label: frontal orienting fields —same-as→ frontal eye fields
span.quote: On the basis of their connectivity with other brain regions and their physiological properties, these had been suggested as analogous or perhaps even homologous to the two key primate regions PPC and FEF, respectively [ 46 , 47 ].

span.label: lateral intraparietal —part-of→ posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: Using monkeys trained to perform a visual perceptual decision-making task in which the experimenters could titrate each trial’s difficulty (“random dot motion discrimination” (RDM) task; [ 23 , 24 ], Shadlen and Newsome found that during the process of decision formation, neurons in the lateral intraparietal (LIP) subregion of posterior parietal cortex (PPC) had firing rates that appeared to ramp up in time.

span.label: secondary visual cortex —distinct-from→ posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: Immediately posterior to the rodent PPC are a set of individually small visual areas, collectively referred to as secondary visual cortex (V2; [ 65 – 67 ]).

span.label: redundant circuit —contrasted-with→ causal circuit
span.quote: While the PPC could, perhaps, play a role in gradual accumulation as part of a much larger redundant circuit in the Poisson Clicks task, it is notable that out of 6 different rat regions probed so far (medial prefrontal cortex and superior colliculus, (Hanks, Yartsev, et al. unpublished data); anterior dorsal striatum and auditory striatum (Yartsev, Hanks, et al., unpublished data); and FOF and PPC), the only region for which silencing has no impact on task behavior is the PPC.

span.label: click-triggered average —part-of→ Poisson clicks
span.quote: First, by computing the click-triggered average firing rate, it was possible to estimate the impact of a single evidence pulse on a neuron’s firing rate.

span.label: decision boundary —part-of→ evidence accumulation
span.quote: In this model, when the evidence is strong, the accumulator’s value quickly diverges away from the decision boundary, and it rapidly become easy to say on which side of the decision boundary it is.

span.label: Inactivating rat posterior parietal cortex left performance on the accumulation task essentially unaffected, despite PPC encoding the graded accumulator value.
span.quote: In contrast to expectations, however, inactivation of the PPC produced entirely negligible effects on performance of the Poisson Clicks task

span.label: The authors conclude that PPC is the least likely of the regions examined to be a genuine node of the accumulation circuit.
span.quote: Consequently, we consider the PPC to have the lowest likelihood of being an important center of the causally relevant circuit for gradual evidence accumulation.

span.label: The serial account in which PPC computes the accumulator and hands it to FOF was falsified by the perturbation results.
span.quote: As we describe below, this serial model turned out to be wrong.

span.label: Frontal orienting fields carry a categorical, step-like read-out of which side of the decision boundary the accumulator is on, rather than its graded value.
span.quote: Thus what is best read out from FOF firing is not the graded value of the accumulator, but rather which categorical decision report the subject should make if the trial ended at that point in time.

span.label: Unpublished data suggest at least one subcortical region meets all three criteria and could be the first identified node of the causal accumulation circuit.
span.quote: Current unpublished data (Yartsev, Hanks, et al.) suggests that while some subcortical regions may be like the FOF in playing an important role in the task, but not in gradual accumulation per se, at least one other subcortical region appears to satisfy all three criteria, and may thus become the first identified node in the causal circuit for evidence accumulation.

span.label: The authors propose a nomenclature reform, restricting the label 'rodent PPC' to tissue whose physiology and connectivity match primate PPC.
span.quote: We advocate reserving the name “posterior parietal cortex (PPC)” in rodents to regions displaying physiological and connectivity profiles similar to those of the primate PPC

span.label: parietal cortex encodes the graded accumulator value and yet silencing it leaves task performance essentially unchanged
span.quote: In contrast to expectations, however, inactivation of the PPC produced entirely negligible effects on performance of the Poisson Clicks task [ 53 ].

span.label: the same inactivations did affect interspersed free-choice trials, so the manipulation itself worked
span.quote: This was the case even while the same inactivations had a large effect on interspersed control “free choice” trials [ 53 ], and even though PPC inactivations have a substantial effect on a different auditory task involving parametric working memory [ 54 ].

span.label: of six rat regions silenced so far, parietal cortex is the only one with no effect on the task
span.quote: the only region for which silencing has no impact on task behavior is the PPC

span.label: tuning curves distinguish two regions whose trial-averaged responses look alike: graded in parietal, step-like in frontal
span.quote: But while tuning curves in PPC were found to be smooth functions of the value of the accumulator --indicating that the graded value of the accumulator could be read out from PPC firing, as also found in the primate PPC [ 51 ]-- the tuning curves in the FOF were much more step-like, with one cluster of firing rates for accumulator values to one side of the decision boundary, and a different cluster of firing rates for values on the other side of the decision boundary (see Fig. 2e ).

span.label: the mapping from accumulator value to firing rate stays fixed across the trial even as the value changes
span.quote: Thus, although the value of the accumulator changes during the course of a trial, the mapping from accumulator value to firing rate does not.

span.label: neither candidate region satisfies all three of the authors' criteria for causal circuit membership
span.quote: As described above, neither the FOF nor the PPC satisfy all three criteria.
